KEY FINDING: total pair error mass is conserved across the entire loss-weight sweep (EXP02 1.5, EXP03 1.25/1.35). Loss weighting only moves the decision boundary along the overlap; it does NOT separate the classes. Only feature engineering can reduce this.
The stable Web-BruteForce precision win comes from here, not from new feature separability.

recommended_exp04.idea: Feature/confusion diagnostic phase FIRST (Option B): quantify the SlowHTTPTest<->FTP feature overlap (and the Web-XSS->Bot/Infiltration leak) using TRAIN/VALIDATION-split processed features only, to decide whether further gains require feature engineering rather than more loss/weight tuning.
recommended_exp04.description: The confusion evidence proves the dominant remaining error (SlowHTTPTest<->FTP, ~14,758 conserved across the whole loss-weight sweep) is feature-limited: loss weighting redistributes the error between the two directions but does not reduce the total. The smaller stuck classes (Web-XSS 38, SQL-Injection 12) are too tiny and too entangled with large classes (Bot, Infiltration) to optimize without overfitting or routing harm. Therefore the responsible next step is a diagnostic, not another blind loss/weight experiment. The diagnostic computes per-feature class-conditional separability between SlowHTTPTest and FTP (and Web-XSS vs Bot/Infiltration) on TRAIN features (with a VALIDATION cross-check), e.g. per-feature distribution overlap / simple separability scores, to answer: is the pair separable with existing features (=> a targeted modeling experiment is justified) or genuinely overlapping (=> only new engineered features, a separate preprocessing-protocol decision, can help). It selects nothing on test.
recommended_exp04.gated_followup_if_separable: cicids_hierarchical_exp05_head2_focal_loss (code change, ~4-6 runs, validation-driven, gated on the diagnostic showing separability)
target_metrics: whether the overlap is feature-limited or model-limited
go/no-go for feature engineering vs a targeted modeling experiment
recommended_exp04.expected_benefit: Prevents wasted controlled-experiment slots on loss/weight tricks that the conservation evidence says cannot work; produces an evidence-based go/no-go for feature engineering; keeps the program honest.
recommended_exp04.expected_risk: Low. It is analysis only (no training, no test tuning). The main risk is that it confirms the pair is feature-limited and the cheap wins are exhausted - which is itself a valuable, honest result that points to promoting EXP03 1.25 with documented weaknesses.

why_selected: Confusion conservation is decisive: the SlowHTTPTest<->FTP total error is ~14,754 (baseline) vs ~14,758 (EXP03 1.25 mean) - loss weighting only redistributes it. More loss/weight/focal/sampler tuning on this pair is predicted by the data to be zero-sum.

The remaining rare-class targets are either feature-limited (the pair) or too small to optimize responsibly (Web-XSS 38, SQL-Injection 12), and the tiny classes leak into LARGE classes (Bot, Infiltration), so up-weighting them risks routing harm for <=21 samples.
EXP03 1.35 seed42 already demonstrated tiny-class instability (SQL-Injection precision 1.0->0.091) under stronger weighting - a warning against the targeted-weight family.

Config-only rare-class levers are effectively exhausted: attack_loss_weight is already optimized at 1.25; the weight method (sqrt_inverse_frequency, cap 10.0) is hardcoded with no per-class override, and the cap is non-binding, so there is no safe config-only rare-class boost left.
A diagnostic is the scientifically honest 'analyze before assume' step the task demands, and it produces the evidence needed to choose between feature engineering and promoting EXP03 1.25.

why_not_selected_now.focal_loss_head2: Plausible modeling lever for hard examples but it is a code change AND, per conservation evidence, unlikely to beat the feature limit on the dominant pair; risks tiny-class instability (1.35 precedent). Justified only if the diagnostic shows separability -> recommend_after_exp04 (as EXP05), gated.
why_not_selected_now.rare_class_or_targeted_weight_boost: No config hook exists (weights are hardcoded sqrt_inverse_frequency, cap 10.0 non-binding), so it needs code; and it would chase 12-38 sample classes entangled with large classes -> high overfit + routing-harm risk. needs_main_control_decision / reject.
why_not_selected_now.slowhttptest_ftp_targeted_weighting: Conservation proves this only shifts error between the two directions; it cannot reduce the pair. reject as an improvement lever.
why_not_selected_now.class_balanced_effective_number_loss: Code change; a reweighting variant unlikely to beat the feature limit. possible_later.
why_not_selected_now.attack_only_sampler: Code change; the hard pair is not rare so limited upside; oversampling tiny classes risks overfit/optimism. possible_later.
why_not_selected_now.validation_only_calibration: A Head-1 routing tool (recovers missed-as-benign); it does NOT change Head-2 family attribution, so it is off-topic for a rare-class task. Still useful as the routing experiment (prior EXP plan), but not a rare-class lever. possible_later.
why_not_selected_now.two_stage_finetuning: Code change, medium complexity; will not beat feature conservation on the pair. possible_later.
why_not_selected_now.specialist_module: Model-zoo; the project requires one organized final system. reject.
why_not_selected_now.promote_exp03_with_warnings: Legitimately on the table - EXP03 1.25 is already a strong, honest improvement (attack +0.0219, rare +0.0576, routing within noise). If the diagnostic confirms the pair is feature-limited, promoting EXP03 1.25 with documented weak classes (Web-XSS, SQL-Injection, SlowHTTPTest/FTP residual) is the honest stop. needs_main_control_decision.

promotion_criteria.note: EXP04 (the diagnostic) does not itself produce a promotable model; it produces a go/no-go. Promotion criteria below apply to any gated modeling follow-up (EXP05) and restate the EXP03 bar.
promotion_criteria.rare_class_macro_f1: >= 0.774 (hold the EXP03 1.25 rare gain; no tiny class -> ~0)
promotion_criteria.dos_slowhttptest_recall: improved without dropping FTP-BruteForce F1 below ~0.770 (the pair must net-improve, not see-saw)
promotion_criteria.robustness: no single seed regresses routing badly; tiny classes (12/38/96) used only as guardrails, never as promotion drivers
promotion_criteria.safety: validation-only selection; train-only weights; single final test per seed; no test tuning; no baseline/EXP01/EXP02/EXP03 overwrite

rejection_criteria: Diagnostic shows the pair is feature-limited AND no modeling lever can net-improve it -> stop modeling; recommend promoting EXP03 1.25 with documented weaknesses.
Any follow-up that improves a macro number only by over-fitting a 12-38-96 sample class, or by trading the SlowHTTPTest/FTP see-saw without net pair improvement.
Any taxonomy change to inflate metrics; any weak-class hiding; any test tuning; any model-zoo proliferation.
